title: Non-blocking finding from PR #274's review (in-place decisions-entry editing convention)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #274 (backend-cftc-cot-data-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. PR #274 amended the already-`done` `backend-cftc-cot-data` task's own `decisions` entry in place (appending clarifying text to the existing `decision` field, without deleting anything) rather than appending a brand-new `decisions` array entry to that task. task-worker recorded a `decisions` entry on the followups task explaining this was appropriate: a narrow, additive factual correction, recoverable via git history, also recorded as a new decisions entry (on the followups task itself) with rationale, and distinct from CLAUDE.md's stricter 'additive-comment-only' rule which specifically targets merged PR *descriptions*, not task-board decisions entries. This reasoning closely mirrors the one existing precedent CLAUDE.md itself endorses for the analogous PR-description case (backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups / PR #227), where an in-place edit was allowed specifically because the task/checklist explicitly called out the description itself as the thing needing correction -- which is also true here (this task's own checklist item said 'Worth a small comment/decisions-text update'). Reviewed and judged a sound, non-blocking call, not a violation of any explicit written rule -- but the `decisions` array's whole structure is designed to be an append-only chronological log (new timestamped entries), and an alternative of appending a brand-new decisions entry to `backend-cftc-cot-data.json` (rather than mutating an existing entry's `decision` field text) would have been an equally discoverable, strictly append-only way to correct the record without ever touching an existing entry's field content -- worth considering as the preferred convention if this situation (correcting a stale claim in an already-done task's decisions entry) recurs, so CLAUDE.md's decision-memory section can eventually be explicit about which of the two patterns (in-place amend vs. new append-only entry) is preferred for a done task's own decisions array, the way it already is for merged PR descriptions.

checklist.step: Decide (and record as a `decisions` entry, ideally on this followup task or as an addition to CLAUDE.md's decision-memory section) whether correcting a stale claim inside an already-`done` task's existing `decisions` entry should default to appending a brand-new `decisions` array entry (strictly append-only, mirroring the array's own design) instead of amending the existing entry's `decision` field text in place -- and if a written convention is added, retrofit this reasoning as precedent alongside the PR #227 case CLAUDE.md already documents for merged PR descriptions.

decisions.decision: Adopted 'append a brand-new `decisions` entry by default' as the written convention for correcting a stale claim inside an already-`done` task's existing `decisions` entry, mirroring (not duplicating) the existing merged-PR-description rule: in-place amendment of an existing entry's `decision`/`rationale` text is permissible only when the correction is a narrow factual correction (not a rewrite of what was actually decided), the original text stays recoverable via git history, the correction is also recorded as a fresh `decisions` entry with rationale, and it doesn't touch code/merge state -- and even then, the append-only default should still be preferred unless the checklist item or task explicitly calls out the existing entry's own text as the thing to fix. Added this as a new paragraph in CLAUDE.md's 'Decision memory (`decisions`)' section (right after the index.json state/path mirror paragraph, parallel in structure to the Autonomous-pipeline section's PR-description rule), and retrofitted PR #274 (backend-cftc-cot-data-followups' in-place amendment of backend-cftc-cot-data.json's cftc_contract_market_code entry) as the precedent for the 'explicit callout' carve-out, the same role PR #227 plays for the PR-description case.
decisions.rationale: The `decisions` array is already structurally an append-only chronological log of timestamped entries (per its own documented shape and CLAUDE.md's own framing of it as such) -- a brand-new entry is self-describing purely from its own timestamp and text, whereas mutating an existing entry's field text (even additively) means a reader can only tell what was originally claimed versus added later by diffing git history, which most readers of a done task's JSON won't think to do. Considered and rejected keeping the two conventions (PR descriptions vs. task decisions entries) governed by entirely separate, unrelated rules with no shared carve-out logic: that would have left PR #274's in-place edit undefended by any written rule (pr-reviewer and pr-decision on PR #274 had to reason it through from first principles by analogy, which is exactly the kind of implicit-precedent gap this task exists to close) and would have missed that the two cases share the same underlying tension (additive-log immutability vs. in-place-readability-at-the-source) and the same resolution shape (default to additive, narrow carve-out when the task itself flags the existing text as broken). Also considered making in-place amendment the default (on the theory that a decisions entry, unlike a PR description, is expected to be edited as understanding evolves) and rejected it: the array's own documented shape has no 'superseded_by'/'amended' field, so an in-place edit with no new timestamp is indistinguishable from the entry always having read that way, silently erasing the append-only audit trail the array's structure is designed to provide -- exactly the failure PR #274's own already-recorded rationale flagged as worth avoiding for the original text (which is why PR #274 itself never deleted anything, only appended within the field). This is an ordinary engineering/documentation-convention judgment call resolvable from the two already-documented analogous cases (PR #227's carve-out, PR #274's own reasoning) plus the array's own documented design intent, not a product decision needing `waiting_input`.

comments.summary: Confirmed genuinely docs/task-board-only: `git diff main...HEAD --stat` shows only CLAUDE.md (+2/-0), this task's own JSON (checklist checked off, decisions entry added, git block added), and index.json's state mirror. No backend/frontend application code touched, so the coverage/lint gates aren't at risk from this diff specifically (still re-ran them for a baseline -- see notes).

The new CLAUDE.md paragraph accurately parallels the existing PR-description convention: both default to append-only, both list the same four carve-out conditions (narrow factual correction, recoverable via history, also recorded as a fresh decisions entry, no code/merge-state touched), and both apply the 'explicit callout' exception only when the checklist/task names the existing text itself as the thing to fix. No contradiction found with any other CLAUDE.md section (the index.json state/path mirror paragraph immediately above, the 'references entry as logical pointer' paragraph immediately below, and the Autonomous-pipeline PR-description bullet it mirrors all remain consistent).

Verified the retrofitted PR #274 precedent against the actual done-task records rather than taking the PR body's claim at face value: docs/tasks/done/backend-cftc-cot-data.json's second decisions entry (the cftc_contract_market_code one) does contain an appended NOTE (not a rewrite) recording the oil/bonds display-name renames, and docs/tasks/done/backend-cftc-cot-data-followups.json's checklist item literally says 'Worth a small comment/decisions-text update' -- matching the new paragraph's characterization exactly, the same 'explicit callout' shape backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups documents for PR #227.

Confirmed the still-unresolved governance question in backend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups-followups-followups (whether a CLAUDE.md/.claude/ edit needs an explicit human touchpoint) remains in `state: waiting_input` with no new decisions entry answering it -- so the existing precedent (PR #229: ordinary pipeline handles it) still applies here, and this PR going through the ordinary pipeline is not itself a violation of anything currently decided.

Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this docs-only PR (which touches no frontend files). A very similar, already-investigated flake on FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx alone is tracked on frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups (still planned) as a one-off suspected environmental fluke; this review's observation (recurrence on a second, unrelated PR, now also affecting a second file, and resolved by disabling file-parallelism specifically) is new evidence worth adding to the board rather than only noting here. Tracked as a new follow-up task (see below) rather than duplicating into that unrelated task chain, since this review's own instructions scope follow-ups to this task's id.
